This mechanism has the key property that my ranking cannot change my set of obtainable schools—it only determines which obtainable school I get, choosing my most preferred one from that set. This is characteristic of a strategy-proof mechanism (like Deferred Acceptance), where truth-telling is a dominant strategy: submitting my true preferences guarantees I get the best possible school among those I could ever obtain, regardless of what others report or my priorities are.

Since misrepresenting my preferences cannot expand my obtainable set and could only cause me to select a worse school from within that set, the optimal strategy is to rank truthfully according to my actual preferences: y > w > z > x.

I don't need to strategize based on my priorities (w:2, x:1, y:2, z:1) or the fact that other applicants favor y > x > w > z, since the mechanism's structure already accounts for these when determining my obtainable set. My only lever is choosing my most preferred option within that set, which truthful ranking achieves optimally.
